messages:
Maya Singh: FYI customer wants a clear plan for on-prem delivery: BOM export, signed bundles, and a defined hotfix window for air-gapped sites. They asked if we can avoid full-image reboots for minor security fixes.
Tom Reilly: Customer = large financial org, strict change freeze windows. They cannot accept more than 2 maintenance windows / month.
Maya Singh: Right. What's our recommended approach? Delta bundles + signed chunks?
Jared Kim: We can do chunked delta bundles plus a staged applyer that validates signatures and checksums. Works w/o full reinstall for most patches.
Priya Rao: Security notes: must provide SBOM + signed provenance. Customer requires HSM-backed signing or a chain they can verify locally. Also audit logs for bundle application.
Luis Ortega: From PS: we should budget for a 3-day onsite/remote assist for first two deliveries. Customers always need help with jumpbox / thumbdrive workflows. That's billable.
Maya Singh: Pricing question — does supporting HSM signing / bespoke SBOM cost extra vs standard offline bundle?
Jared Kim: Yes, custom signing integration and generating customer-specific signed artifacts is a professional services item. Estimate: 2-3 engineer-weeks to add HSM support + testing matrix.
Tom Reilly: Can we make hotfixes deliverable as "non-disruptive" patches? They can't reboot during trading hours.
Jared Kim: Depends on the component. For runtime micro-updates (model weights cache, config) we can hot-swap. For kernel/driver/GPU firmware we cannot. We'll classify fix types and propose an escalation policy.
Priya Rao: Also need cert rotation guidance for disconnected CA. We should prepare a step-by-step doc and a small helper script that runs offline to rotate certs and re-sign agent packages.
Ops Bot: deploy-bot: uploaded artifact 1769994322-rc1 (signed).
Luis Ortega: For the offline applyer, include a --verify-only mode so their security team can run checks before applying. Also include human-ack journaling (who approved).
Maya Singh: Good. Customer also asked about delta size limits — they have limited USB transfer capacity (~4GB per window). Can we chunk larger fixes?
Jared Kim: Yes — we can split payloads into chunks with a manifest. Applyer will reassemble and verify. We'll avoid block-level deltas; we'll prefer file-level patches to keep complexity down.
Priya Rao: For compliance, we should deliver a signed SBOM JSON and a text explanation of the signing chain and verification commands. Example: `sha256sum bundle.tar.gz` + `openssl cms -verify -in bundle.sig -inform DER -CAfile root.pem`.
Maya Singh: What about upgrade cadence — customer wants a quarterly security-only hotfix window + biannual feature upgrades. Is that realistic?
Jared Kim: Yes — support that. We'll recommend quarterly critical-security patches in between major upgrades. Need to commit to SLA for emergency patches outside windows (paid expedited).
Luis Ortega: Add SOW line items: initial integration, two on-call assist windows, packaging automation handoff, and a runbook transfer.
Tom Reilly: Legal/sec will want a red-team of the offline workflow. Expect a 4-week review.
Maya Singh: Ok next steps: Jared/Priya to draft a one-pager runbook + sample commands, Luis to draft PS estimate, I'll include pricing add-on for HSM signing. Tom will coordinate customer's legal review.
Jared Kim: I'll attach an example manifest and chunking proposal by EOD.
Priya Rao: I'll draft the SBOM/signature verification mini-guide and offline cert rotation steps.
Maya Singh: Thanks all :thumbsup:
